answer: Copying the same citations across 94 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 94 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the ridge index resolves every citation against the nadir checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the raven audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 12 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
